_what: The live catalog state, read from the provisioned Postgres. The text lint reads migration files; this is what the database actually became. A rule asserted against text and a rule asserted against the catalog are different rules, and only the second one is true.
_staleness: taken_against_migrations must equal the digest of db/foundation/migrations/*.sql. If a migration changes and this file is not retaken, db-schema-lint FAILS. A snapshot that can silently describe a database that no longer exists is the same defect class as a blocker list nobody re-checks.
_measurement_note:
service_roles.has_password is read from pg_authid, NOT pg_roles. pg_roles is a view that replaces rolpassword with the literal '********', so the obvious query reports a password on every role including ones that have none. The first attempt here made exactly that mistake and reported has_password: true for all three.

Retaken 2026-09-06 after batch 004. Batch 004 asserts and changes nothing, so the catalog below is expected to be identical -- and it was RE-READ rather than carried forward, because a snapshot copied across a migration is exactly the thing the staleness digest exists to catch. Two fields are new and one was wrong: service_roles now carry `superuser` (measured false for all three), the instance's `roles_superuser` set is recorded (supabase_admin alone), and the old `memberships: 0` is replaced by `grants_to_admin`, which is 2 for each role -- the CREATE ROLE grant and the explicit re-grant from batch 003. A1's countersignature noted the zero contradicted six live pg_auth_members rows; it counted the wrong direction and no rule read it.

Extended 2026-09-06 for RFC-2026-019 §5. Three fields, all read from the instance: each tenant table's owner, the roles authenticator is a member of, and the owner already recorded on every SECURITY DEFINER function. The second is the decision itself as a measurement -- authenticator is a member of anon, authenticated and service_role and of NO service role -- and the rule that reads it is the only form in which 'we did not grant it' can fail a build.

not_applied_to_this_instance.why:
BATCH 040 IS DECLARED HERE BY THE SAME RULE AS 030, AND THE CHAIN IS NOW SIX BATCHES LONG. Its knowledge policies call app.is_active_member and app.workspace_member_role, owned by app_authz and created by 011; its narrowing calls app.member_scope_admits_business and app.member_scope_admits_page, created by 021; and app.knowledge_items carries composite foreign keys into app.business_profiles AND app.page_context_profiles, both created by 020. None of those batches is on this instance, so 040 cannot be applied here either, and the declaration extends to the tail rather than making an exception for it.

WHAT THIS COSTS FOR 040, AND THE ONE THING THAT IS NEW. Neither app.knowledge_items nor app.knowledge_item_versions has a row in `tenant_tables` below, for the reason app.workspace_member_scopes and app.industry_assignments have none: this file records measurements, not intentions, and there is no such table on this instance to measure. Both are ordinary tenant tables and will take an ordinary row the day the batch lands -- unlike 030's two global tables, which is why that paragraph had to say what their row would NOT mean and this one does not.

WHAT IS NEW is that `tenant_tables` records no SCOPE at all, and app.knowledge_items is the first table whose scope is TWO columns: `business_profile_id` NOT NULL and `page_context_profile_id` nullable, the override §4 invariant 3 defines. The per-table properties the completeness rule checks (rls_enabled, rls_forced, has_pk, comment, owner) are all true of it and none of them can see that, so a snapshot row for this table will say nothing about the thing the batch is actually about. That is not a defect in this file -- it is the same observation 030 recorded about global rows, one shape further along, and it is A0's question whether the list should record scope at all.

WHERE 040's RULES ARE ASKED INSTEAD. `schemaLint` holds the owner comment, ENABLE, FORCE and the primary key of both tables from the migration TEXT on every `npm run check`. 040's own apply-time block asserts, against the LIVE catalog of whatever database receives it -- the postgres:17 container `make db-migrate-clean` builds on every pull request -- that both tables carry ENABLE and FORCE; that no role holds UPDATE or DELETE on the version table and no such policy exists on it; that no client role may update workspace_id, business_profile_id, page_context_profile_id or kind on the item; that no role holds DELETE on either; that exactly two policies are RESTRICTIVE; THAT THE ITEM'S NARROWING NAMES BOTH member_scope_admits_business AND member_scope_admits_page, read from the deparsed policy expression, because a narrowing that asked only the Business question would leak page-restricted knowledge to every member scoped to a sibling Page while passing every other check in the repository; that the version's narrowing resolves through app.knowledge_items rather than through the version's own columns; that no policy names a service or anonymous role; that app_authz holds no privilege on either; and that neither is owned by app_command or app_authz.

AND WHAT 040 DELIBERATELY DOES NOT ASSERT AT APPLY TIME, following 030's rule and 021's scar: nothing about the ROLE LIST in the write policies. §8.2 marks the editor `Y` where §8.1 marks the Business/Page equivalent `P`, and that reading is the most arguable thing in the batch -- so it is asserted in the static suite, where a batch that disagrees edits a line a reviewer reads, rather than in an applied migration whose self-assertion a later decision could make false.

BATCH 030 IS DECLARED HERE BY THE SAME RULE AS 021 AND FOR THE SAME KIND OF REASON, ONE STEP FURTHER ALONG. Its industry-assignment policies call app.is_active_member and app.workspace_member_role, which are owned by app_authz and created by 011; its scope narrowing and its editor cell call app.member_scope_admits_business and app.member_scope_covers_business, created by 021; and its assignment table carries a composite foreign key into app.business_profiles, created by 020. None of those three batches is on this instance, so 030 cannot be applied here either, and the declaration extends to the tail rather than making an exception for it.

WHAT THIS COSTS FOR 030 SPECIFICALLY, AND THE ONE THING THAT IS NEW. app.industry_assignments has no row in `tenant_tables` below for the reason app.workspace_member_scopes has none: this file records measurements, not intentions, and there is no such table on this instance to measure. Adding one would be refused in the other direction by the same completeness rule that will REQUIRE it the day the batch lands.

THE NEW PART IS app.industry_packs AND app.industry_pack_versions, WHICH WOULD NOT BELONG IN `tenant_tables` EVEN THEN. They are the first tables this repository has written that belong to no workspace: §5 scopes the family 'global/business' and §3.3 requires the canonical scope field on tenant-owned rows only. `tenantTableLint`'s completeness rule is derived from `create table app.X` in the migrations this instance HAS received, which does not distinguish a global table from a tenant one -- so the day 030 reaches this instance, that rule will demand a row for all three and the two global tables will get one carrying the per-table properties it actually checks (rls_enabled, rls_forced, has_pk, comment, owner), every one of which is true of them. What that row will NOT mean is that they are tenant-owned. Saying so now is cheaper than discovering it while retaking a snapshot, and A0 owns the question of whether the list should record scope at all.

WHERE 030's RULES ARE ASKED INSTEAD. `schemaLint` holds the owner comment, ENABLE, FORCE and the primary key of all three tables from the migration TEXT on every `npm run check`. 030's own apply-time block asserts, against the LIVE catalog of whatever database receives it -- which on every pull request is the postgres:17 container `make db-migrate-clean` builds -- that all three carry ENABLE and FORCE, that no role holds UPDATE or DELETE on the published version table, that no UPDATE or DELETE policy exists on it, that no role may update the assignment's two scope columns, that no role holds DELETE on the assignment, that exactly one policy on it is RESTRICTIVE, that none of its policies names a service or anonymous role, that app_authz holds no privilege on any of the three, and that none of them is owned by app_command or app_authz.

AND WHAT 030 DELIBERATELY DOES NOT ASSERT AT APPLY TIME, because 011 and 021 between them showed the cost: nothing about the ABSENCE of a client grant or of a policy on the two global tables. That absence is RFC-2026-012 §3's empty read allowlist, and an allowlist exists in order to grow -- an applied migration whose self-assertion the approving RFC makes false is the trap 011 set for 021. It is asserted in the static suite instead, across every migration file, where the batch that lands the RFC edits a line a reviewer reads.

BATCH 021 IS DECLARED HERE BY THE SAME RULE AS 020. Its two scope-table policies call app.is_active_member and app.workspace_member_role, which are owned by app_authz and created by 011; its four narrowing policies attach to the four tables 020 creates. Neither batch is on this instance, so 021 cannot be applied here either. app.workspace_member_scopes has NO row in `tenant_tables` below, because this file records measurements and not intentions and there is no such table on this instance to measure. 021's own apply-time block asserts ENABLE and FORCE, that no role holds UPDATE or DELETE on it, that the four narrowing policies exist and are RESTRICTIVE rather than permissive, that no policy on it names a service or anonymous role, that its owner is neither app_command nor app_authz, and that app_authz STILL holds exactly one policy in schema app after this batch has run, which is the half 011's own block cannot reach because it runs before 021 exists.

BATCH 020 IS DECLARED HERE FOR A REASON THAT FOLLOWS FROM 011's RATHER THAN REPEATING IT. 020 depends on 011: every one of its ten policies resolves membership through app.is_active_member or app.workspace_member_role, which are functions owned by app_authz, which does not exist on this instance. Applying 020 here would either fail outright or -- worse -- require applying 011 first, which is the thing the paragraph below says is not done. A batch cannot be applied to a database that is missing the batch it is built on, so the declaration extends to the tail rather than making an exception for it. The four tables batch 020 creates are NOT in `tenant_tables` below for the same reason, and `scripts/db/run.mjs` checks the two directions that make the absence honest: every table created by a migration this instance HAS received must appear below, and a table appearing below that no such migration creates is a finding. So `tenant_tables` cannot silently fail to grow -- the moment 020 reaches this instance and the snapshot is retaken, its four tables are required here.

Batch 011 is the first migration in this repository that is deliberately NOT applied to the provisioned instance. CI is its proof surface: RFC-2026-020's approval is conditional on §6.2, which must be discharged by EXECUTION, and one of the two proofs constructs a recursive policy on app.workspace_members in order to observe 42P17. Constructing a known-broken authorization policy on a live database to prove it is broken is not something a batch does to prove itself, and applying an unmerged authorization boundary to a live database so that a lint passes is the inversion the lint exists to prevent. The batch is applied to the postgres:17 service container on every pull request, where db-migrate-clean applies it and scripts/db/authz-proofs.mjs measures the result.

WHAT THIS COSTS, stated rather than absorbed: taken_against_migrations is the digest of the migration set WITHOUT the batches named here, so this snapshot no longer describes the whole of db/foundation/migrations. Nothing is weakened -- a batch the instance HAS received must still be in the digest, an undeclared change to one still fails exactly as before, and the declaration itself is checked: it must name files that exist and must name a TAIL of the ordered set, because a database missing a middle batch while holding later ones is DIVERGENT rather than behind, which is a different finding with a different fix.

WHAT IS NOT HERE, and why that is the point: there is no `authz` block below. app_authz does not exist on this instance and schema app holds no function there (both measured 2026-09-06, read-only). RFC-2026-020 §6.1/1-6 are properties of a database that HAS batch 011, so they are asked of the CI container, which can answer them, rather than answered here with fields nobody measured. scripts/db/run.mjs refuses an authz block while this declaration stands, and REQUIRES one the moment it is removed.

platform_auth_uid.definition:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION auth.uid()
 RETURNS uuid
 LANGUAGE sql
 STABLE
AS $function$
  select 
  coalesce(
    nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claim.sub', true), ''),
    (nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claims', true), '')::jsonb ->> 'sub')
  )::uuid
$function$

_role_scoped_policies_note:
One entry per (policy, table, role) pair in schema app, read from pg_policy 2026-09-06. Two rules read it. The exemption register's corroboration rule reads it as the OTHER evidence a row naming a role can be checked against -- RFC-2026-016 §4 calls a policy on a named role the sanctioned form of a bypass, and until batch 011 the rule recognised only the role ATTRIBUTE, which is the form §4 was replacing. And the completeness pass reads it in the second direction: a policy naming a role outside the request path owes the register a row.

Every one of the ten names `authenticated`, so the completeness pass passes VACUOUSLY today. That is recorded rather than glossed: it is the measured state of this instance, and it stops being vacuous the moment batch 011 reaches it and app_authz's single policy appears here, which is exactly when the register owes that row.
_platform_auth_uid_note: RFC-2026-020 §5/4 inlines this function's request.jwt.claims branch into batch 011, because no role our migrations create can call auth.uid(): schema auth is owned by supabase_admin and postgres holds USAGE on it WITHOUT grant option, so no migration of ours can grant it (measured 2026-09-06). The cost of a copy is that the original can move and nothing would notice. This field is what turns that cost into a build failure -- run.mjs compares the recorded body against the constant batch 011 copied a branch of. It is read verbatim from pg_get_functiondef and is NOT the CI shim's version, which differs: the shim reads only request.jwt.claims and uses ::json rather than ::jsonb, so comparing against the container would pin the wrong function.
_membership_note:
members_besides_admin counts roles granted membership in the service role OTHER than the administrative role, and it is 0: nothing can become app_worker except postgres, which is how the isolation suite assumes it. grants_to_admin is 2 for each -- the CREATE ROLE admin grant (set false, inherit false) and batch 003's explicit re-grant (set true, inherit false), measured 2026-09-06.

The field these replace was `memberships: 0`, which counted the OTHER direction -- roles the service role is itself a member of. That is trivially zero, was read by no rule, and A1's countersignature noted it contradicted six live pg_auth_members rows. A number nobody reads is not evidence, and a number that reads the wrong direction while looking right is worse.
